review: The print gives stanza 1 as three lines (the acclamation twice, then the thrice-repeated 'soon') and stanzas 2–4 as four lines; the payload follows the print, so `hebrew-meter.mjs` reports the shape 3/4/4/4 as irregular by construction.

2:1 יִמְחֶה אֲדֹנָי הַדְּמָעוֹת — Revelation 21:4 (וּמָחָה אֱלֹהִים כָּל־דִּמְעָה); the Arabic سَوْفَ يَمْسَحُ رَبِّي الدُّمُوع is the title of the hymn, and Hebrew keeps the plural tears with the singular verb, as the psalm does in Ps 116:8.

2:2 לֹא בֶכִי בַּגְּבוּלוֹת הָהֵם — 'no weeping in those borders', for لَا بُكَاءَ فِي تِلْكَ الرُّبُوع; רְבָעִים is 'quarters/regions', and גְּבוּלוֹת is the biblical word for the territories of the age to come.
4:1 נֵחָטֵף אֶל־הֶעָנָן — 1 Thessalonians 4:17 (נֵחָטֵף … בָּעֲנָנִים); the Arabic سَوْفَ نُخْطَفُ عَلَى السَّحَاب is that verse, and עָנָן is kept singular as in the epistle.

4:2–4:3 וְנִשְׁמַע קוֹל הַבְּרָכָה / בְּבֵית הָאָב — John 14:2 (בְּבֵית אָבִי); the Arabic صَوْتَ التَّرْحَاب / فِي بَيْتِ الْآب is the welcome in the Father's house, and בְּרָכָה carries the greeting without the modern Hebrew שָׁלוֹם עֲלֵיכֶם.
4:4 נִלְבַּשׁ בִּגְדֵי לָבָן — Revelation 7:9 (לְבוּשִׁים בִּגְדֵי לָבָן); the Arabic بِيضَ الثِّيَاب is that clothing.
